'''Lillian-Yvonne Bertram''' is an American poet known for their work on poetry and [[digital storytelling]].

== Education and career ==
Bertram holds a PhD in Literature & Creative Writing from the [[University of Utah]],<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Personal science|url=https://www.worldcat.org/title/personal-science/oclc/%7B%7B%7B946964339%7D%7D%7D|date=2015|language=English|first=Lillian-Yvonne|last=Bertram}}</ref> in addition to degrees from [[Carnegie Mellon University]]<ref name="CMU" /> and the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Poetry Foundation|date=2020-01-07|title=Lillian-Yvonne Bertram|url=https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poets/lillian-yvonne-bertram|access-date=2020-01-07|website=Poetry Foundation|language=en}}</ref> Bertram is an associate professor at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]].<ref name="faculty page">{{cite web|title=Lillian-Yvonne Bertram|url=https://english.umd.edu/directory/lillian-yvonne-bertram|access-date=29 August 2024|website=University of Maryland Department of English|publisher=University of Maryland}}</ref>

== Writings ==
Bertram is known for their work on poetry, African-American poetry, poetics, digital storytelling, digital and computational poetics, media arts, and pedagogy. Their first book, ''But a Storm is Blowing From Paradise'' is a series of poems that make note of mental and physical landscapes that portray the connection with body, space, time, and love.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bertram |first1=Lillian-Yvonne |title=But a storm is blowing from paradise : poems |date=2012 |publisher=Red Hen Press |location=Pasadena, CA |isbn=9781597091688 |edition=1st}}</ref>

Bertram has published other books including ''Personal Science'', a work that explores some occurrences that can result from obsessive thinking.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bertram|first=Lillian-Yvonne|title=Personal science|date=2017|isbn=978-1-936797-91-2|edition=|location=North Adams, Massachusetts|oclc=962750135}}</ref> In April 2016, ''a slice from the cake made of air,'' was published and it processes the physical and mental trauma of abortions, as well as sexual desire and contemporary culture.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bertram|first=Lillian-Yvonne|title=A slice from the cake made of air|date=2016|publisher=Red Hen Press|isbn=978-1-59709-565-5|edition=|location=Pasadena, CA|oclc=961415861}}</ref> Published on December 1, 2019, ''Travesty Generator'' consists of poetry generated using an open-source coding and presents how the black experience has become homogenized, branded, and codified for the dissemination by capitalism.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bertram |first1=Lillian-Yvonne |title=Travesty generator |date=2019 |location=[Blacksburg, Virginia] |isbn=978-1-934819-84-5}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2011, Bertram received the [[Benjamin Saltman]] Poetry Award for their book ''But a Storm Is Blowing from Paradise''.<ref name="CMU">{{Cite web|last=Carnegie Mellon University|date=March 22, 2011|title=Alum Lillian-Yvonne Bertram Wins Award for Poetry Collection|url=http://www.cmu.edu/dietrich/english/news-and-events/news-archive/2011/alum-lillian-yvonne-bertram-wins-award-for-poetry-collection.html|access-date=2022-01-11|website=www.cmu.edu|language=en}}</ref> Bertram was the 2015 recipient of a National Endowment for the Arts Creative Writing Poetry Fellowship,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lillian-Yvonne Bertram|url=https://www.arts.gov/impact/literary-arts/creative-writing-fellows/lillian-yvonne-bertram|access-date=2022-01-11|website=www.arts.gov|language=en}}</ref> and the 2017 recipient of the Harvard University Woodberry Poetry Room Creative Grant.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Woodberry Poetry Room Creative Fellowship|url=https://library.harvard.edu/grants-fellowships/woodberry-poetry-room-fellowship|access-date=2022-01-11|website=Harvard Library|language=en}}</ref> In 2020 Bertram received the Anna Rabinowitz Prize for ''Travesty Generator'',<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 18, 2020|title=Announcing the 2020 Anna Rabinowitz Prize winner, Lillian-Yvonne Bertram|url=https://poetrysociety.org/about/news/announcing-the-2020-anna-rabinowitz-prize-winner-lillian-yvonne-bertram|access-date=2021-05-04|website=Poetry Society of America|language=en}}</ref> which was also a nominee for the [[National Book Award for Poetry]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Williams|first1=John|date=18 September 2020|title=National Book Awards Names 2020 Nominees|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/09/18/books/national-book-awards-long-list-nominees-2020.html|access-date=11 January 2022}}</ref>
